name: Centre for Aquaculture Progress: electrical stunning for farmed fish in Greece (Ambitious Impact, 2023 idea report)
summary: Ambitious Impact's 2023 estimate for a new charity advocating for Greek legislation requiring farmed sea bream and sea bass to be electrically stunned before slaughter, with corporate campaigns as first steps, as a way into EU fish welfare policy. Greece is the EU's largest fish producer. The idea the Centre for Aquaculture Progress was founded to run. A re-implementation of AIM's spreadsheet, traced from its welfare points per dollar of charity costs (334; the report rounds to 330), with the discounting over 60 years rebuilt from the yearly rows. The result rests on AIM's welfare gain per fish, the mean of two estimates 46 times apart: 3.17 points for a fish's whole life and 0.0685 counting only the slaughter (with a tenfold weight for intense suffering). AIM's Guesstimate version of the same model gives far less: 20 welfare points per dollar (1.7 to 48) in the report, 210 (3.3 to 250) in the sheet. Not counted in the sheet: the 25% chance the report gives that the EU requires stunning anyway. Welfare points have no exchange rate to the site's scale, so a bridge of ours turns them into days of a fish's pain, weighed by Rethink Priorities' welfare range for fish.

source.title: Influencing EU fish welfare policy through strategic work in Greece (CE 2023 preventative animal advocacy report): CEA
source.license: AIM terms of use: non-commercial use and citation with attribution; no open licence found

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Ambitious Impact's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost.

sections.title: From welfare points to days of pain (ours)
sections.explainer: charityevals' bridge, not Ambitious Impact's. Ambitious Impact's welfare points (used until 2023) count one point of an animal's welfare score (−100 to +100) for one year, times its chance that the animal is sentient. We take the sentience discount out (Rethink Priorities' weights below already include it) and turn each welfare-point-year into days of disabling pain on the animal's own scale (shared figure, with a range).

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' species step, the same for every animal model: days of pain for each species, weighed by how much it can suffer relative to a chicken (Rethink Priorities).

rows.label: Inputs – costs: Discount rate (Expected)
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact discounts future costs and welfare points at 0.04 a year. Linked to the shared discount rate (Your values); the evaluator view pins it to Ambitious Impact's rate.

rows.label: Years the reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: reads the shared "Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway" (5 by default), like every model that credits a won reform. Ambitious Impact counts the fish welfare reforms for every year of its sheet once it takes effect, years 6 to 60 (55 years), as if it would never have come otherwise; that span is kept as the evaluator's and used in the evaluator view. The five years until it takes effect and every year counted are discounted at "Next year's good counts less by", as Ambitious Impact's sheet does.

Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this grant's breakdown.

rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Welfare points affected per dollar you give
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact's welfare points per dollar, times the share of the full cost paid in cash.

rows.label: Welfare points per dollar you give, before the sentience discount: farmed fish
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact's welfare points per dollar you give with its probability that the fish are sentient (52.6%) divided back out, so the sentience discount isn't applied twice: Rethink Priorities' welfare range for fish, below, already includes it.

rows.label: Days of disabling pain spared per dollar you give: farmed fish
rows.explainer: Welfare-point-years for farmed fish times the days of disabling pain one welfare-point-year stands for (shared figure: 2.1, range 1.09 to 9.09, calibrated on Ambitious Impact's own welfare points and suffering-adjusted days for hens moved out of battery cages). These are the animals' own days, before weighing by species. The bridge from welfare points to days of pain (2.1, 1.09 to 9.09) is our judgment, not Ambitious Impact's figure (facts: aim_wp.pain_days_per_wp_year, kind judgment).

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give: farmed fish
rows.explainer: The days of pain for farmed fish, weighed by how much fish can suffer relative to a chicken (Rethink Priorities; mean of carp and salmon). The fish weight is a stand-in, our judgment: Rethink Priorities estimated only carp and salmon, and their mean stands for every farmed and wild-caught fish (facts: welfare_ranges.fish_vs_chicken, kind judgment).

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give
rows.explainer: Days of disabling pain spared, all species, counted as a chicken's. The headline converts this into years of healthy life with the chicken slider and the healthy hours lost per day of disabling pain.

output.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give

theoretical.reason: Ambitious Impact's estimate of the idea, written before the charity existed; not based on the charity's own results.
theoretical.runs: The Centre for Aquaculture Progress works on electrical stunning of sea bream and sea bass, now through certifiers (GLOBALG.A.P., ASC) and producers rather than Greek legislation, which AIM modelled.
